findings.title: Denial cache keys collide when resource fields contain underscores
findings.body: The key concatenates namespace, user, action, resource name, and parent folder with underscores but does not encode or delimit the fields unambiguously. For example, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key. A cached denial for one check can therefore deny a different resource check for the same user/action for up to the cache TTL. Use an unambiguous encoding or include lengths/separators that cannot occur in values.

findings.title: Denial cache is shared across identity types
findings.body: The denial key uses `checkReq.UserUID` but not `checkReq.IdentityType`. Different identity types can have the same UID (for example, a user and service account), while their permissions are resolved differently. A denial cached for one identity can therefore incorrectly deny another identity with the same UID, namespace, action, name, and folder. Include the identity type in the key.

findings.title: Cached denials survive permission grants until expiry
findings.body: A denial is cached for the full short-cache TTL, and the denial-cache lookup returns before checking current permissions. If a resource is granted to the user after a denial is cached, the user continues to be denied for up to 30 seconds even though permissions were updated. This undermines the stated goal of making newly created resources accessible and can also delay legitimate access grants; invalidate matching denial entries when permissions change or avoid caching denials where permission state can change.
